model: Broker FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (bank-style, net debt held at zero, engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: 7,756,694,797 shares in issue (A + H), unchanged since the 2020 A-share placement; FY2025 annual report line 31 and the EPS note (line 12191-12215). No share option or restricted-share scheme, so basic = diluted. Held FLAT: perpetual subordinated bonds are equity-classified but non-converting, and their cost is charged through the leakage path, not the share count.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme or expense disclosed in the FY2025 annual report (state-controlled A+H broker; Beijing Financial Holdings, Central Huijin, CITIC Financial Holdings). SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in RMB (CNY) millions; H-shares quote in HKD. fx_rate 1.1748 HKD per CNY (model -> quote), Yahoo CNYHKD=X at the same timestamp as the price. No parity check available: the A-share (601066.SS, CNY 22.93 at the same time, ~HKD 26.9) trades ~2.5x the H-share on a common-currency basis -- CSC carries one of the widest A/H premia among mainland brokers -- so the A line is a reference, not a check. The model does not assume the discount closes.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY in CNY, because the flows are FCFE (profit attributable to ordinary shareholders less retained capital) and the model holds net debt at zero. China 10-year CGB ~1.8% + 6.5% equity risk premium for a mainland financial x beta 1.3 (H-share beta to HSI ~1.2-1.4; earnings are pro-cyclical with A-share turnover and 25% of FY2025 revenue is mark-to-market investment income, with an -RMB8.6bn derivatives line inside it) = 10.25%, rounded up to 10.5%. Same rate as CITIC Securities (6030.HK) and China CITIC Bank (0998.HK): CSC is smaller and more investment-banking-weighted than CITIC Securities, but its risk coverage ratio is 206% of risk capital reserves, net capital RMB83bn, and it has no NPL book; a higher rate would charge cycle risk twice, since the margin/growth paths and the probability weights already carry it. Same rate in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (RMB436m current + RMB461m non-current at FY2025, note 35) are immaterial against RMB860bn of assets and their cost is inside the pre-tax margin; not deducted again. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders. The engine's PBT x (1 - rate) must land on common NI, so cash_tax_rate_path is the combined leakage on PBT of income tax + non-controlling interests + DISTRIBUTIONS TO PERPETUAL SUBORDINATED BOND HOLDERS (equity-classified, charged to retained earnings, already deducted in the company's EPS): FY2023 27.7% (tax 1,324 + NCI ~13 + perpetuals 984 on PBT 8,372), FY2024 29.2% (1,455 + 12 + 1,067 on 8,690), FY2025 28.1% (2,283 + 15 + 999 on 11,737), H1 2026 27.7% (2,182 + 2 + 536 on 9,821). Income tax alone runs 17-19% (tax-exempt fund and government-bond income against the 25% statutory rate). The perpetual balance has grown to RMB38.2bn (H1 2026) so the distribution is ~RMB1.2-1.4bn/yr going forward; as a FIXED charge it is a smaller share of a boom-year PBT and a larger share of a trough-year PBT, which is why the leakage path is lower in FY2026 and higher in the bear case. NCI equity (RMB42m) is immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: securities-broker FCFE capitalised at cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF engine with the bank mapping used on 6030.HK (CITIC Securities, valued 2026-10-23), 1788.HK, 0998.HK, 2016.HK, WF and LYG. ROUTING: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes financial institutions away from the owner-FCF DCF; a broker-dealer's reported operating cash flow (FY2023 -10.1bn, FY2024 +1.1bn, FY2025 +42.7bn, H1 2026 -22.4bn) swings with repo, margin-loan and client balances and says nothing about owner earnings, and 'net debt' (CSV total_debt RMB175.5bn of borrowings/bonds/short-term financing vs cash 66.8bn, plus client brokerage deposits) is balance-sheet funding, not a claim to deduct from an earnings-based value. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenue (fee + interest + investment income, CSV 'Revenue'; FY0 = FY2025 RMB34,985m, the new presentation basis under which FY2024 was restated from 32,216 to 30,140); ebitda_margin_path = PRE-TAX PROFIT margin (da, sbc and lease paths = 0 so EBIT = PBT); cash_tax_rate_path = tax + NCI + perpetual-bond distribution leakage (see nci_treatment); capex_pct_path = EARNINGS RETAINED to grow the common equity base and regulatory net capital (the broker's reinvestment), set so terminal retention x terminal ROE = terminal growth; wc_capture_pct = 0. FCFE = common NI - required retention = dividend capacity. The company's ACTUAL payout is lower than this capacity (FY2025 DPS RMB0.34 = 31% of EPS 1.09; FY2024 RMB0.255 = 32%; H1 2026 interim RMB0.29 = 32% of H1 EPS 0.92) - it has been compounding common book at 6-8%/yr and earning ~9-10% ROE on it, roughly its cost of equity, so the surplus retention is treated as value-neutral and the FCFE is credited as if distributable (same convention as 6030.HK). last_fcf = FY2025 common NI 8,440.9 (attributable 9,439.4 less perpetual distributions 998.5) less retention required for 5.5% growth on opening common equity 76,643 (4,215) = 4,226; FY2025 cash dividends actually paid were 2,560. NET DEBT = 0 by the bank convention. No SBC. PERPETUAL BONDS: RMB38.2bn of equity-classified perpetual subordinated bonds (note 43) are EXCLUDED from common equity (per-share book is RMB11.29 on RMB87.6bn, not RMB16.21 on RMB125.7bn) and their distributions are charged in the flows - once each, no double count. MID-CYCLE: reported weighted-average ROE FY2021-25 was ~15.9/10.0/8.6/8.2/10.5% (5y avg ~10.6%, FY2022-25 avg ~9.3%); H1 2026 ROE ~8.3% unannualised (~16-17% annualised) is a cycle high on near-doubled A-share turnover and is NOT the run-rate. The pre-tax margin history (FY2021 33.4%, FY2022 26.0%, FY2023 24.6%, FY2024 28.8% restated, FY2025 33.5%, H1 2026 42.5%) is faded to 30% through-cycle in the base case.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Common-equity 3y CAGR 6.7% vs revenue 3y CAGR -1.4%: the gap exceeds 30% because FY2022 was a post-boom year (revenue fell 9%) while book kept compounding on ~68% retention; the equity rate is a retention effect, not a growth signal, and the driver paths fade to 3% nominal rather than using it.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs from FY2022->FY2025 (3y) and FY2020->FY2025 (5y). 'equity' is COMMON equity (attributable equity less equity-classified perpetual bonds): FY2020 57,774, FY2022 68,338, FY2025 82,957; the headline attributable equity CAGRs (8.5% 3y, 12.0% 5y) are inflated by RMB26bn of perpetual issuance over the period. 'fcf' CAGRs are on profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders (NI less perpetual distributions: FY2020 9,139, FY2022 6,655, FY2025 8,441), the FCFE numerator, not reported FCF, which is meaningless for a broker-dealer. Both 5y rates are negative because FY2020 was itself a boom year (PBT 12.1bn): the 3y rates are trough-to-peak, the 5y rates peak-to-peak, which is the cleanest statement of through-cycle growth -- roughly flat earnings, 2-3% revenue, book growing by retention.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +25% (~RMB43.7bn): H1 2026 revenue 23.1bn (+41.8% YoY); H2 2025 was 18.7bn, so an H2 2026 of ~20.6bn (above H2 2025 but below the H1 2026 peak as turnover eases) gives +25%. Then the cycle turns: -8% and -3% in FY2027-28 as A-share turnover, margin balances and investment-income marks normalise from a near-doubled-turnover year, back to 4% nominal (wealth-management AUM, China Fund, China Securities International) fading to 3%.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin. FY2026 39% vs H1 2026 actual 42.5% (operating leverage on a trading boom, H2 lower); FY2027 33% (= FY2021/FY2025 boom-year level); then 30% through-cycle, one point above the FY2021-25 average of ~29% (33.4/26.0/24.6/28.8/33.5) because scale, the international arm and the AM/wealth fee mix have risen since the 2022-23 trough.
base.capex_note: Retained earnings as % of revenue. FY2026 10.4% = ~RMB4.5bn = 36% of common NI (12.5bn) = 5.5% common-equity growth on 83.0bn (payout capacity ~64% vs actual ~32%: the gap is surplus retention credited to FCFE, see inputs.notes). Glides to 7.2% of revenue = 34% of terminal NI (NI = 30% x 0.70 = 21.0% of revenue) so that retention x terminal ROE ~8.75% = terminal growth 3.0%; terminal common equity/revenue ~2.4x as today.

bull.growth_note: FY2026 +33% (~RMB46.5bn): H2 2026 runs at H1's pace. Only a shallow -3% dip in FY2027 because capital-market reform (National Nine Articles, pension pillars, Stock Connect flows) keeps turnover structurally higher and the IB pipeline (HK IPO sponsorship after CATL, SOE capital raises, M&A advisory No.1 by count) stays full; 5% nominal thereafter fading to 3.5%.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: 33% through-cycle = the FY2021/FY2025 boom-year level held permanently: consolidation-driven share gains, the international arm (revenue >100% YoY in FY2025) and the wealth/AM fee mix lift the margin four points above the historical average.
bull.capex_note: Terminal retention 7.4% of revenue = 32% of NI (NI = 33% x 0.705 = 23.3% of revenue); retention x terminal ROE ~11% = 3.5% growth. Implied payout ~68%.

bear.growth_note: FY2026 +15% (~RMB40.2bn): H2 2026 falls back to ~17.1bn, below H2 2025 (a policy move to cool speculative trading, or a market reversal that flips the FVTPL marks). FY2027 -20% and FY2028 -8% replay the FY2021-23 post-boom decline (revenue -7% then -7%, PBT -27% then -12%) at a harsher amplitude; 2-3% nominal thereafter.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin falls to 27%/25% (FY2023 trough was 24.6%) and settles at 27%: fee-rate reform caps brokerage and fund fees, merged rivals (Guotai Haitong, CICC+Dongxing+Cinda) take underwriting share, the derivatives book (-RMB8.6bn line in FY2025) reverses, and the enlarged funding bill (borrowings RMB146bn at FY2025) sits against a smaller revenue base.
bear.capex_note: Terminal retention 6.5% of revenue = 36% of NI (NI = 27% x 0.67 = 18.1% of revenue); retention x terminal ROE ~7% = 2.5% growth. Leakage 33% because the ~RMB1.3bn perpetual distribution is a fixed charge against a smaller PBT. ROE well below cost of equity means value sits well below book.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 is the cycle peak: revenue +25% to ~RMB43.7bn on H1's +42%, pre-tax margin 39%, common profit ~RMB12.5bn (ROE ~15% on the RMB83bn common base). FY2027-28 give back 11% of revenue as A-share turnover, margin balances and investment-income marks normalise, the margin settles at 30% (a point above the FY2021-25 average, held by scale, the international arm and the fee-mix shift), and growth fades to 3% nominal. Through-cycle ROE ~9% versus a 10.5% cost of equity, so fair value sits a little under common book (RMB11.29/sh, ex the RMB38bn of perpetuals): the FCFE stream of ~RMB5-7bn/yr capitalised at 7.5% (10.5% - 3%). The business compounds common book at 3-5% while paying out ~65% of earnings in capacity terms; actual payout is ~32% and the surplus is credited as value-neutral retention.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2025-26 upswing is the start of the structural re-rating Beijing is engineering: consolidation toward ~10 leading institutions with CSC a designated 'first-class investment bank' by 2030, pension pillars past RMB1tn, Stock Connect flows, and China Securities International (CATL sponsor) taking international revenue to a meaningful share. Revenue +33% in FY2026 with only a shallow FY2027 dip, a 33% through-cycle pre-tax margin, ROE ~11%, terminal growth 3.5%. CSC earns above its cost of equity, so the value moves above common book -- still far below where the A-share (~2x book) trades.
scenario_narratives.bear: The boom reverses: a policy move to cool speculative turnover, or a market fall that flips the proprietary and derivatives book's marks. Revenue -20% in FY2027 and -8% in FY2028 (a harsher replay of FY2022-23), pre-tax margin 25-27%, fee-rate reform and the merged rivals cap the recovery at 2.5% growth, and the RMB38bn of perpetual bonds become a heavier fixed charge on a smaller PBT. ROE ~7% against a 10.5% cost of equity: the FCFE stream is ~RMB3-4bn and the common equity is worth ~0.5x book, the 2023-24 trough rating for the sector.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25, the same weighting as the sibling broker 6030.HK. The upside (structural reform plus consolidation leadership, a top-3 IB franchise with state deal flow) and the downside (cycle reversal from a near-doubled-turnover year with a mark-to-market trading book as the largest revenue line, and faster-growing merged rivals) are both real and roughly equally likely from a cycle-high starting point; the state parents remove the solvency tail but not the earnings tail, so no tilt either way.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A broker's value is its through-cycle return on equity against its cost of equity, not a snapshot of a boom year. CSC Financial is a top-3 Chinese investment bank with state parents and a strong underwriting franchise, and it has earned ~9-10% on common equity across the last cycle -- about its cost of equity -- so fair value is close to common book (RMB11.29/sh after stripping RMB38bn of equity-classified perpetual bonds, whose distributions are charged in the flows). FY2026 earnings (likely ~RMB12-13bn to common, ROE ~15%) are a cycle high built on near-doubled A-share turnover, and the model fades them rather than capitalising them. The H-share at ~0.8x common book and ~6-7x FY2026E earnings prices a cycle reversal; the A-share at ~2x book prices the reform story and a scarcity premium. The valuation sits at the H-share, not between.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle reversal: 25% of FY2025 revenue was mark-to-market investment income (with an -RMB8.6bn derivatives line inside it) and brokerage commissions move one-for-one with A-share turnover; a market fall reverses both (bear case -20% revenue in FY2027).
Policy: CSRC levers on IPO pace, margin rules, stamp duty and fund fee-rate reform can cut brokerage, IB and AM revenue abruptly, as they did in 2022-23.

Retention earning below cost of equity: actual payout ~32% means the company keeps compounding common book at 6-8%/yr while the balance sheet grows faster (+27% total assets in H1 2026, risk coverage 236% -> 207%); if the retained capital earns 7% rather than 9-10%, value falls toward the bear case regardless of the cycle.

Perpetual bonds: RMB38bn of equity-classified perpetuals (44% of common equity) carry a fixed ~RMB1.3bn/yr distribution that is senior to ordinary dividends; the model treats them as a leakage on PBT, and a trough year makes that charge a larger share of earnings.

Consolidation: a forced merger (CSC has been a recurring subject of tie-up speculation with CITIC Securities, unconfirmed) would bring dilution and integration risk; merged rivals could take underwriting share.
Currency: value is built in CNY and bridged at 1.1748 HKD/CNY; CNY depreciation lowers the HKD value one-for-one.
A/H discount: the H-share trades at ~40% of the A-share's common-currency price; the model does not assume the discount closes, and H-share supply (16% of capital) is thin.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 6066.HK at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 10.18-14.35. CNYHKD=X and 601066.SS from the same API at the same time.
data_sources.financials: 6066.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2017-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2023-FY2026 interims; RMB millions). H1 2026 PBT, equity, perpetual bonds and distributions from 6066.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (lines 474, 543-547, 3690-3699, 4481, 5613-5639). PBT 5-year table, ROE, tax, perpetual distributions and dividends from 6066.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (lines 1294, 1337, 1423, 9439, 12180, 12191); FY2020-23 perpetual distributions from the FY2021/FY2023 statements of changes in equity.
